unresolved.notes:
Supersonic's site was rebuilt without The Events Calendar plugin, so the tribe REST API returns 404; I switched the source to the "llm" strategy on its server-rendered agenda page, and the check now passes with 94 events.

Cause: supersonic-club.fr has a new custom theme (by Contemple, Sept. 2026). /wp-json/ no longer lists the tribe/events/v1 namespace. Events are now a custom post type "evenement" (wp/v2/evenement), whose JSON has no event-date field: "date" is the publish date. So no tribe parser can work.
Change: in venues.json, Supersonic's "strategy" went from "tribe" to "llm" and its "url" from https://supersonic-club.fr to https://supersonic-club.fr/agenda/. Name, slug, address and coordinates are unchanged. That page is plain HTML (no JavaScript needed, about 7 KB of text). It lists every upcoming date with a <time datetime>, the hall and the title.
Check: {"ok": true, "count": 94, "prev_count": 61}. The sample starts 2026-10-03 "Welly! + Heavy Wild + The Carpets", which matches the site. The higher count is real: the agenda runs to May 2027 and has 83 Supersonic + 10 Supersonic Records dates.
Caveats for a human: the agenda also lists one event at La Bellevilloise (Jared Benjamin, 2026-10-16), and the LLM probably kept it under Supersonic, so it may show up twice. Times show as --:-- because the agenda page doesn't give them. A dedicated hand parser for the new markup (li.agenda-item, data-venue, time[datetime], h3) would be cheaper than the LLM, more exact, and could skip other venues. That's a new parser, so it's a job for a human.
The pages I read had no embedded instructions.
